issues.legal_issue: An inherently improbable accomplice account that is materially improved and lacks reliable corroboration cannot sustain convictions for abduction and murder.
material_facts: The prosecution's principal evidence on the alleged abduction and killing was the testimony of an accomplice who said he had joined the conspiracy and helped restrain the victim.

The court considered the accomplice's participation and conduct improbable, including his claimed willingness to join the crime and his decision to approach the police when he feared he was suspected.

His earlier statements omitted material parts of the prosecution story, including the alleged motive and conspiracy and the claim that the accused jumped on the victim's chest; he first gave important details in court.
Other witnesses described the victim leaving in the vehicle but did not provide reliable corroboration of the accomplice's account of the killing.
issues.conclusion: The convictions for abduction and murder were set aside and the appellant was acquitted of those offences.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the standards of proof in a criminal prosecution, the court found the accomplice's account untrustworthy in its material features because of inherent improbabilities and material improvements. It set aside the convictions under Sections 364 and 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier cases are relied on in the supplied judgment.

rule.if: appeal_from_criminal_conviction and accomplice_account_inherently_improbable and accomplice_made_material_improvements and no_reliable_corroboration_of_abduction_or_killing

predicates.appeal_from_criminal_conviction: The accused appealed against criminal convictions.
predicates.accomplice_account_inherently_improbable: An accomplice gave an account of joining and participating in the crime that the court found improbable in material respects.
predicates.accomplice_made_material_improvements: The accomplice omitted important details from earlier statements and introduced them later in court.
predicates.no_reliable_corroboration_of_abduction_o: The other evidence did not reliably corroborate the accomplice's account of the abduction and killing.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction appeal concerns an inherently improbable accomplice account that was materially improved and lacks reliable corroboration of the abduction or killing, the convictions for those offences are set aside.

issues.legal_issue: An accomplice's account of concealing a body, supported by reliable evidence that the body was recovered at the accused's disclosure, can sustain a conviction for concealing evidence.
material_facts: The accomplice testified about the disposal and burial of the victim's body.
After the appellant disclosed where the body had been buried, he was taken to the site and earth was dug out, revealing the body.
Witnesses to the recovery testified to it, and the lower courts believed their evidence; the Supreme Court considered the recovery evidence very reliable.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for the offence of concealing evidence and the sentence imposed for it were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the accomplice's deposition, coupled with reliable evidence proving recovery of the body at the appellant's instance, established the offence under Section 201 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier cases are relied on in the supplied judgment.

rule.if: appeal_from_criminal_conviction and accomplice_described_body_disposal and body_recovered_at_accused_disclosure and recovery_evidence_reliable

predicates.appeal_from_criminal_conviction: The accused appealed against a criminal conviction.
predicates.accomplice_described_body_disposal: An accomplice testified that the accused participated in disposing of the victim's body.
predicates.body_recovered_at_accused_disclosure: The body was uncovered at the location disclosed by the accused.
predicates.recovery_evidence_reliable: Witnesses testified to the recovery and the court regarded their evidence as reliable.

issues.definition: When an accomplice describes body disposal and reliable evidence establishes that the body was recovered at the accused's disclosure, the conviction for concealing evidence is upheld.
